# Backglow

> Backglow is a free, open-source (GPL-3.0) macOS app that provides ambient lighting for Mac displays: it reads the edges of the screen in real time and sends their colors over USB to an ESP32 or ESP8266, which drives a WS2812B LED strip behind the monitor. It works like Ambilight on Philips TVs but is an independent DIY project, not affiliated with Philips.

Key facts:

- Platform: macOS 26 or later. The signed and notarized download (current version 3.0.2) is for Apple silicon Macs; Intel Macs on macOS 26 can build it with Xcode 26.
- Hardware: WS2812B strip (GRB color order, up to 255 LEDs), ESP32 Dev Module (data on GPIO 18) or NodeMCU ESP8266 (data on D1), 5 V power supply. Firmware for both boards is in the repository and is flashed with PlatformIO.
- Connection: USB serial at 230,400 baud. No Wi-Fi, no WLED support, no server or web interface.
- Processing: ScreenCaptureKit capture, Metal shader averaging in linear light, letterbox detection, spring smoothing, anti-flicker filter, color calibration, minimum backlight and power limit. Up to 60 frames per second. The techniques follow HyperHDR, reimplemented in Swift.
- The LED layout and colors can be stored on the controller and load automatically on the next connection.
- Privacy: runs entirely on the Mac, makes no network connections, no telemetry.
- Languages: English and German.
- Author: Jan de Boer.
